# Adjudication Task — Chapter 350

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃350화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저벅. 저벅.
  6|
  7|나는 오늘도 어김없이 짬통을 들고 걸음을 옮겼다.
  8|
  9|지하 뇌옥에서의 시간은 느릿느릿했지만, 한편으로는 국방부 시계만큼이나 꾸준히 흘러갔다. 벌써 엿새째에 접어든 뇌옥에서의 일상도 점점 익숙해지고 있었다.
 10|
 11|덜컹. 끼이이익.
 12|
 13|녹슨 창살을 열고 오물과 구정물이 고인 뇌옥 안으로 성큼 들어갔다.
 14|
 15|형틀에 묶여 있는 노인이 히죽거리는 웃음으로 나를 반겼다.
 16|
 17|“왔느냐?”
 18|
 19|정마대전 당시 마교에 합류해 백 명이 넘는 정파 무림인을 죽였다는 살귀다.
 20|
 21|이제 이빨 빠진 노인이 된 그는 부정확한 발음으로 말을 이었다.
 22|
 23|“내 마지막으로 말하건대…….”
 24|
 25|나는 기다란 국자로 짬을 퍼담으며 말을 잘랐다.
 26|
 27|“어제도 마지막이라면서?”
 28|
 29|“이번엔 진짜 마지막이다.”
 30|
 31|“그래, 이렇게 말해 놓고 내일이 진짜 진짜 마지막이겠지.”
 32|
 33|엿새 동안 무수하게 겪은 일이다. 새삼스럽지도 않다.
 34|
 35|내 무신경한 태도에 순간 움찔했던 노인이 외쳤다.
 36|
 37|“너, 내 제자가 되어라!”
 38|
 39|“너, 맞아라.”
 40|
 41|빡!
 42|
 43|국자에 정수리를 얻어맞은 노인이 고통에 몸부림친다. 그의 사지를 결박한 쇠사슬이 출렁이며 요란한 소리를 냈다.
 44|
 45|“크아아악!”
 46|
 47|“소리 줄여. 시끄러워.”
 48|
 49|“끄윽. 이놈이!”
 50|
 51|고래고래 소리를 지르려던 노인이 문득 눈을 동그랗게 뜨고 코를 벌름거렸다. 뇌옥 안의 악취에 가려져 있던 기름 냄새를 맡은 것이다.
 52|
 53|“이, 이 냄새는 뭐냐?”
 54|
 55|“알 거 없어.”
 56|
 57|“오리 구이. 오리 구이구나! 혹시 술도 있느냐?”
 58|
 59|“술은 무슨.”
 60|
 61|“거짓말! 이 주향은 틀림없는 검남춘(劍南春)이다!”
 62|
 63|“……이 정도 후각이면 마약 탐지견 수준인데.”
 64|
 65|“내놓거라! 어서!”
 66|
 67|빡!
 68|
 69|“끄아아악!”
 70|
 71|“임자 있는 거야. 짬이나 처먹어.”
 72|
 73|나는 짬통을 내려놓고 마지막 뇌옥을 향해 이동했다.
 74|
 75|다른 뇌옥들에 비해 유난히도 깊고 어두운 그곳에는 낯익은 괴인이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
 76|
 77|덜컹.
 78|
 79|“식사 가져왔습니다.”
 80|
 81|“…….”
 82|
 83|“기다리느라 힘드셨죠? 그나저나 여긴 왜 이렇게 춥나 몰라. 잠자리 많이 불편하실 텐데 당문에 부탁해서 가죽 이불이라도 깔아 드릴까요?”
 84|
 85|“…….”
 86|
 87|역시 이렇게 나오는군.
 88|
 89|고양이 발바닥처럼 부드러운 말투에도 괴인, 천력마는 묵묵부답으로 일관했다.
 90|
 91|사흘 전, 그 일이 있고 난 후부터 천력마는 눈을 감고 입을 닫았다.
 92|
 93|물론 이렇게 나온다고 해서 포기할 내가 아니지.
 94|
 95|“자자. 그러지 마시고. 이것 좀 드셔 보십쇼.”
 96|
 97|나는 기름에 젖은 면지를 꺼내어 펼쳤다.
 98|
 99|각종 향신료를 발라 알맞게 구워 낸 오리 한 마리가 탐스러운 자태를 드러낸다. 악취까지 몰아낼 만큼 먹음직스러운 향기는 덤이다.
100|
101|“이게 무엇이냐, 전직 황실 숙수님이 만드신 오리 구이인데, 나도 먹어 보니까 오리가 확실히 연해. 맛도 굉장히 안정적이야.”
102|
103|“…….”
104|
105|“오리 구이에는 또 술이지. 사천의 명주라는 검남춘! 천력마 대협과 같은 영웅호걸에게는 술과 고기가 어울리지. 안 그래요?”
106|
107|“…….”
108|
109|가뜩이나 한기가 맴도는 뇌옥 안에 싸늘한 침묵이 내려앉았다.
110|
111|가부좌를 취한 천력마를 활짝 웃으며 바라보던 나는 결국 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
112|
113|“시벌, 못 해 먹겠네.”
114|
115|사흘 동안 온갖 비위를 맞춰 줬다. 말투도 나긋나긋한 존댓말로 바꾸고, 인의 대협이라고 치켜세워 주며 알랑방귀도 뀌었다.
116|
117|그러나 천력마는 내가 제안하는 모든 제안과 편의를 거부했다. 음식이며, 각종 옷가지며 갖다 바쳐 봤자 손끝 하나 대지 않았다.
118|
119|“이 정도면 할 만큼 한 것 같은데. 진짜 이렇게 나올 거야?”
120|
121|“…….”
122|
123|“내가 인격자라 이렇게 신사적으로 대해 주는 거지, 사천당문 쪽에서 알게 되면 어떻게 될까. 응?”
124|
125|그때, 조용히 가부좌를 튼 채 눈을 감고 있던 천력마가 입을 열었다. 장장 사흘 만에 듣는 그의 목소리는 잔뜩 쉬어 있었다.
126|
127|“그리해라.”
128|
129|“뭐?”
130|
131|“고문이라면 이미 질릴 만큼 겪은 몸. 설령 이승을 떠난다 해도 여한은 없느니라.”
132|
133|지하 뇌옥에 갇힌 지 사십여 년. 해탈한 스님처럼 초연한 천력마의 모습에 나는 혀를 찼다.
134|
135|“거 참. 말 한번 더럽게 안 통하네. 암천에 대해 알고 있는 대로만 말해 달라는 게 그렇게 어려운 부탁인가?”
136|
137|“할 말은 모두 했다. 노부를 죽이든 고문하든, 네 녀석이 알아서 하거라.”
138|
139|“아니, 무슨 이런 노인네가 다 있어.”
140|
141|하지만 천력마의 입술은 이미 굳게 닫혀 있었다. 그리고 아마 다시는 열리지 않을 것이다.
142|
143|“……노인네 고집하고는.”
144|
145|땅이 꺼져라 한숨을 내쉰 나는 그의 손이 닿는 곳에 술과 오리 구이를 내려놓고 돌아섰다.
146|
147|“일단 알겠으니까, 그건 먹읍시다. 당신 사흘 동안 아무것도 안 먹었잖아.”
148|
149|말하면서도 알고 있다. 내일, 모레, 혹은 사흘 뒤에 온다 해도 내가 준 음식들은 처음 모습 그대로 차갑게 식어 있을 거라는 사실을.
150|
151|“빌어먹을.”
152|
153|천력마를 끝으로 배식을 끝마친 나는 뇌옥에서 멀리 떨어진 복도에 털썩 주저앉았다.
154|
155|‘천력마.’
156|
157|형용할 수 없는 눈빛, 딱딱하게 굳은 그의 얼굴이 눈앞을 어른거린다. 그건 분명히 암천이라는 두 글자가 불러일으킨 동요였다.
158|
159|무슨 사정인지 암천에 관해서는 입도 벙긋 안 해서 문제지만.
160|
161|‘하지만 오래전부터 암천을 알고 있었다는 건 확실하지.’
162|
163|천력마의 입으로 직접 듣지 못했을 뿐, 그건 이미 기정사실이나 다름없다.
164|
165|문제는 그가 암천을 어떻게, 어디까지 알고 있느냐는 것이다.
166|
167|나는 지금으로부터 사흘 전, 천력마와 나눴던 대화를 천천히 되짚기 시작했다.
168|
169|내신 7등급의 두뇌를 풀가동해서 나온 결론 중 가장 가능성 있는 추측은 하나뿐이었다.
170|
171|‘암천과 마교는 아주 깊은 연관이 있다.’
172|
173|아니, 어쩌면 한 몸통일지도 모른다.
174|
175|과거 마교의 장로였으며, 지하 뇌옥에서 사십 년간 갇혀 고문을 당하면서도 교에 대한 충성심을 잃지 않은 천력마의 침묵이 그 증거다.
176|
177|‘암천이 마교의 적이었다면 진작 입을 열었겠지.’
178|
179|그럼 암천은 도대체 뭘까. 마교에서 갈라져 나온 일종의 지파(支派)? 아니면 마교 내부에서 만들어 낸 또 하나의 조직?
180|
181|‘신천지의 지파인 병 신천지. 뭐 그런 개념인가.’
182|
183|좌우지간 전염병 같은 새끼들인 건 확실하다.
184|
185|그렇게 한참이나 골똘히 생각에 잠겨 있던 그때, 달달한 냄새와 함께 청풍이 경쾌한 걸음으로 나타났다.
186|
187|“으이!”
188|
189|“……느그 할배 화산 연화봉 살제.”
190|
191|입에 든 것을 꿀꺽 삼킨 청풍이 대답했다.
192|
193|“아닌데요! 지금은 하남에 계시는데요!”
194|
195|“어, 그래.”
196|
197|내가 너랑 무슨 말을 하겠냐.
198|
199|청풍의 품에 산더미처럼 쌓여 있는 음식들을 보니 기가 찼다. 얼굴도 본 적 없는 전직 황실 숙수가 불쌍해질 지경이다.
200|
201|“이거 때문에 나갔던 거야?”
202|
203|“네! 그리고 겸사겸사 개방에서 보낸 서신도 가져왔어요.”
204|
205|“……보통은 그 반대 아니냐?”
206|
207|“헤헤.”
208|
209|“웃지 마. 정들어.”
210|
211|퉁명스럽게 대꾸한 나는 청풍이 내미는 서신을 받아들었다.
212|
213|평소 어디에 보관해 놨던 건지, 때가 꼬질꼬질하게 낀 종이를 펼치자 누런 개털 세 가닥이 스르륵 떨어진다.
214|
215|‘삼결 제자. 분타주가 보낸 거네.’
216|
217|내 예상대로 서신은 개방의 성도 분타주가 궁기방의 앞으로 보낸 것이었다.
218|
219|물론 궁기방은 신의의 비처(秘處)에 있으니, 편한 대로 내게 보낸 거겠지.
220|
221|잠시 후, 서신에서 눈을 뗀 내게 청풍이 물었다.
222|
223|“뭐래요?”
224|
225|“별거 없어. 계속 수색 중이라는 내용이지 뭐.”
226|
227|처음 신의를 찾아내기 위해 사천을 이 잡듯 뒤지던 개방은 목표를 바꿨다.
228|
229|바로 독왕과 경천신니를 시해한 흉수가 그들의 새로운 목표였다.
230|
231|‘하긴, 그렇게 쉽게 잡힐 리가 있나.’
232|
233|사천당문의 힘으로만 해결하겠다던 당사독도 만독지환을 빌려준 이후부터 태도가 바뀌었다.
234|
235|그러나 당문의 적극 협조에도 놈의 행적은 유령처럼 사라져 버린 후였다.
236|
237|“찾을 수 있을까요?”
238|
239|“글쎄, 좋은 결과가 있기를 바라야지. 개방이야 두말할 것도 없고, 척후와 추살의 전문가들인 당문 녹영대까지 있으니 뭐라도 나오지 않겠어?”
240|
241|“관군은요?”
242|
243|“관군도 뭐, 나름대로 제 역할을 톡톡히 하고 있는 것 같던데.”
244|
245|상산왕 주표의 후광은 대단했다.
246|
247|사천성주 원균은 신의 대신 흉수를 찾아 달라는 내 부탁을 흔쾌히 받아들였다.
248|
249|관군들 개개인의 무력은 무림인에 비할 바가 아니지만, 무려 수천 명이나 되는 머릿수는 무시할 게 못된다.
250|
251|“와아! 수천 명이요?”
252|
253|“나도 정확한 숫자는 잘 모르겠는데, 여하간 바글바글한다더라고. 청 소협도 관군 본 적 있지? 사천당문으로 다시 돌아오는 길에.”
254|
255|“아, 그런데 그때 봤던 분들은 그렇게 많지 않던데요.”
256|
257|“……당연하지. 그럼 수천 명이 한꺼번에 몰려다니겠어?”
258|
259|정해진 편제대로 삼삼오오 모여 검문 검색을 실시하는 관군들의 모습을 떠올리는 건 어렵지 않았다.
260|
261|
262|
263|관군, 수색 영역을 서서히 넓혀 청성과 아미로 이동 중.
264|
265|흉수를 찾는 동시에 모종의 사태에 대비하기 위함으로 보임.
266|
267|
268|
269|서신의 마지막 줄까지 읽은 나는 피식 웃었다.
270|
271|‘생각보다는 잘해 주고 있네.’
272|
273|사천성주 허균. 겉모습만 보면 영락없는 탐관오리인데, 아주 무능하진 않은 모양이다. 아니면 이번 임무를 맡은 군관이 능력이 좋든가.
274|
275|‘그나저나 이렇게 하고도 못 찾으면 어떡하나.’
276|
277|당사독에게 큰소리쳐 놓은 게 있다 보니 심히 걱정된다.
278|
279|물론 그 전에 적천강이 무사히 회복하는 것이 먼저겠지만.
280|
281|여전히 굳게 닫힌 치료실을 힐끗 바라본 나는 청풍에게 넌지시 말을 건넸다.
282|
283|“음식 뭐뭐 챙겨 왔어?”
284|
285|“지짜 마아요!”
286|
287|“……입에 있는 거나 마저 먹어. 그냥 내가 알아서 먹을게.”
288|
289|
290|
291|* * *
292|
293|
294|
295|장일은 개방의 이결 제자다.
296|
297|개방도가 된 것은 선택보다는 필요에 의해서였다. 개방에서 정식으로 입방식을 치르고 정식 제자가 되면, 만두 하나를 준다는 소문을 들었기 때문이었다.
298|
299|나흘 동안 굶은 여덟 살짜리 새끼 거지가 뭘 알겠나.
300|

“Waiting must’ve been hard. Why is it so cold in here, anyway? You must be terribly uncomfortable when you sleep. Should I ask the Tang Clan to lay down a fur blanket for you?”

[P42]
“……”

[P43]
So this was how he wanted to play it.

[P44]
Despite my soft, gentle tone, as soothing as a cat’s paw, the Heavenly Power Demon remained stubbornly silent.

[P45]
Ever since what had happened three days ago, he had kept his eyes and mouth firmly closed.

[P46]
Of course, that wasn’t enough to make me give up.

[P47]
“Come on, don’t be like that. Try some of this.”

[P48]
I took out a sheet of grease-stained paper and unfolded it.

[P49]
A whole duck, coated in spices and roasted to perfection, revealed itself in all its plump glory. As a bonus, its mouthwatering aroma was strong enough to drive away the stench of the cell.

[P50]
“What do we have here? Roast duck prepared by a former imperial chef. I tried some myself, and the meat’s definitely tender. The flavor is impressively well-balanced too.”

[P51]
“……”

[P52]
“And you can’t have roast duck without liquor. Jiannan Chun, one of Sichuan’s finest! Meat and liquor are only fitting for a great hero like the Heavenly Power Demon, don’t you think?”

[P53]
“……”

[P54]
A frigid silence settled over the already chilly cell.

[P55]
I kept smiling brightly at the Heavenly Power Demon as he sat cross-legged. At last, I let out a deep sigh.

[P56]
“Fuck, I can’t do this anymore.”

[P57]
For three days, I’d bent over backward to please him. I’d softened my voice, spoken with scrupulous politeness, praised him as a Great Hero of benevolence and righteousness, and kissed his ass shamelessly.

[P58]
But the Heavenly Power Demon had refused every offer and comfort I provided. No matter how much food or clothing I brought him, he never touched any of it.

[P59]
“I’ve done more than enough by now. Are you really going to keep this up?”

[P60]
“……”

[P61]
“I’m only being this courteous because I’m such a gentleman. What do you think will happen if the Sichuan Tang Clan finds out, huh?”

[P62]
At that moment, the Heavenly Power Demon finally spoke without opening his eyes. It was the first time I’d heard his voice in three whole days, and it had grown terribly hoarse.

[P63]
“Tell them.”

[P64]
“What?”

[P65]
“This old man has endured enough torture to be sick of it. Even if I depart this world, I will have no regrets.”

[P66]
He had spent more than forty years imprisoned in the underground prison. Faced with his serene detachment, like some enlightened monk, I clicked my tongue.

[P67]
“Good grief. You really don’t listen, do you? Is it so difficult to tell me what you know about Dark Heaven?”

[P68]
“I have said all there is to say. Kill this old man or torture him. Do as you please.”

[P69]
“What kind of stubborn old man are you?”

[P70]
But the Heavenly Power Demon had already sealed his lips again. He probably wouldn’t open them a second time.

[P71]
“…Stubborn old bastard.”

[P72]
I heaved a sigh deep enough to sink the earth, placed the liquor and roast duck within his reach, and turned away.

[P73]
“Fine. For now, just eat that. You haven’t had anything in three days.”

[P74]
Even as I spoke, I knew. Whether I returned tomorrow, the day after, or three days from now, the food would still be exactly where I’d left it, stone cold and untouched.

[P75]
“Damn it.”

[P76]
With the Heavenly Power Demon fed—or at least served—I finished my rounds and dropped to the floor in a corridor far from the cells.

[P77]
*The Heavenly Power Demon.*

[P78]
His rigid face and that indescribable look in his eyes kept flashing through my mind. There was no mistaking the agitation those two words—*Dark Heaven*—had stirred in him.

[P79]
The problem was that he refused to say a word about it.

[P80]
*But he definitely knew about Dark Heaven long ago.*

[P81]
I hadn’t heard him admit it himself, but it was already as good as established fact.

[P82]
The real question was how he knew about Dark Heaven, and how much he knew.

[P83]
I slowly retraced the conversation I’d had with the Heavenly Power Demon three days ago.

[P84]
After putting the brain that had earned me Grade 7 school marks into overdrive, I arrived at a single plausible conclusion.

[P85]
*Dark Heaven and the Demonic Cult are deeply connected.*

[P86]
No. They might even be one and the same.

[P87]
The Heavenly Power Demon had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult. Even after forty years of imprisonment and torture, he had never lost his loyalty to the Cult.

[P88]
His silence was proof enough.

[P89]
*If Dark Heaven were an enemy of the Demonic Cult, he would’ve talked by now.*

[P90]
Then what the hell was Dark Heaven? Some splinter faction that had broken away from the Demonic Cult? Or another organization created within the Demonic Cult itself?

[P91]
*Like a Shincheonji branch called Sick-cheonji. Something like that.*

[P92]
Whatever they were, one thing was certain: the bastards were a plague.

[P93]
I’d been lost in thought for quite some time when Cheongpung appeared with a spring in his step, trailing a sweet aroma behind him.

[P94]
“Hey!”

[P95]
“…Your grandpa lives on Lotus Peak at Huashan, right?”

[P96]
Cheongpung swallowed what was in his mouth before answering.

[P97]
“No! He’s in Henan right now!”

[P98]
“Yeah, sure.”

[P99]
Why did I even bother talking to him?

[P100]
The mountain of food piled in Cheongpung’s arms left me speechless. I was starting to feel sorry for the former imperial chef, and I’d never even seen the man’s face.

[P101]
“You went out for all this?”

[P102]
“Yes! And while I was at it, I brought a letter from the Beggars’ Sect.”

[P103]
“…Shouldn’t that be the other way around?”

[P104]
“Hehe.”

[P105]
“Don’t smile. I might get attached.”

[P106]
I answered gruffly and accepted the letter Cheongpung held out.

[P107]
When I unfolded the grimy paper—wherever he’d been keeping it, it couldn’t have been clean—three strands of yellow dog hair drifted out.

[P108]
*A three-knot Disciple. The branch leader sent it.*

[P109]
Just as I’d expected, the letter was addressed to Gung Gibang from the Beggars’ Sect’s Chengdu branch leader.

[P110]
Of course, Gung Gibang was at the Divine Physician’s secret refuge, so the branch leader had probably sent it to me for convenience.

[P111]
A moment later, when I looked up from the letter, Cheongpung asked, “What does it say?”

[P112]
“Nothing much. They’re still searching.”

[P113]
The Beggars’ Sect had originally combed through Sichuan with a fine-tooth comb in search of the Divine Physician, but it had since changed targets.

[P114]
Now it was hunting the culprit who had murdered the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.

[P115]
*Not that a man like that would be easy to catch.*

[P116]
Tang Sadok had initially insisted on settling the matter with the Sichuan Tang Clan’s strength alone, but his attitude had changed after he lent me the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P117]
Yet even with the Tang Clan’s full cooperation, the culprit’s trail had vanished like a ghost.

[P118]
“Do you think they’ll find him?”

[P119]
“Who knows? We’ll have to hope for the best. We have the Beggars’ Sect, and the Tang Clan’s Green Shadow Squad are experts in reconnaissance and pursuit. Surely they’ll turn up something.”

[P120]
“What about the government troops?”

[P121]
“They seem to be pulling their weight too.”

[P122]
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, wielded tremendous influence.

[P123]
Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, had readily agreed to my request to search for the culprit instead of the Divine Physician.

[P124]
The individual fighting ability of the government troops couldn’t compare to that of Murim warriors, but their sheer numbers—several thousand men—couldn’t be ignored.

[P125]
“Wow! Thousands?”

[P126]
“I don’t know the exact number, but apparently they’re swarming all over the place. You saw the government troops too, didn’t you, Young Hero Cheong? On our way back to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P127]
“Oh, but there weren’t that many when I saw them.”

[P128]
“…Of course not. Did you think thousands of men would all travel together?”

[P129]
It wasn’t hard to picture the government troops conducting inspections and searches in small groups according to their assigned formations.

[P130]
> The government troops are gradually expanding their search area and advancing toward Qingcheng and Emei.
>
> They appear to be searching for the culprit while preparing for a possible incident.

[P131]
I read the last line of the letter and let out a quiet laugh.

[P132]
*They’re doing better than I expected.*

[P133]
Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, looked every inch the corrupt official, but apparently he wasn’t completely incompetent. Either that, or the military officer in charge of this operation knew what he was doing.

[P134]
*But what if they still can’t find him after all this?*

[P135]
I’d talked a big game in front of Tang Sadok, so the thought was seriously worrying.

[P136]
Of course, Jeok Cheongang’s safe recovery came first.

[P137]
I glanced at the treatment room, whose door remained firmly shut, then casually asked Cheongpung, “What kind of food did you bring?”

[P138]
“Sho mush!”

[P139]
“…Finish what’s already in your mouth. I’ll just look for myself.”

[P140]
* * *

[P141]
Jang Il was a two-knot Disciple of the Beggars’ Sect.

[P142]
He had become one out of necessity rather than choice. He’d heard a rumor that anyone who formally joined the Beggars’ Sect, underwent the initiation ceremony, and became an official Disciple would receive a whole dumpling.

[P143]
What could an eight-year-old beggar brat who hadn’t eaten in four days have known?

[P144]
Clutching his empty stomach, he had gone to the Chengdu branch and become a Beggars’ Sect disciple that very day.

[P145]
“They only gave me half a dumpling, too. Just thinking about it still makes me grind my teeth. Goddamn bastards.”

[P146]
The beggars listening to Jang Il yawned quietly. They’d already heard the story dozens of times.

[P147]
More than ten years had passed, but Jang Il’s anger had yet to subside.

[P148]
“I gritted my teeth over that half dumpling and worked my way up to deputy branch leader. So you lot should…”

[P149]
As the story showed signs of dragging on, the three one-knot Disciples exchanged glances.

[P150]
“Oh! My stomach!”

[P151]
“Gasp! Mine too!”

[P152]
“Ugh, the latrine! Where’s the latrine?”

[P153]
“You little bastards!”

[P154]
Jang Il shouted, but the three beggars had already bolted.

[P155]
“Those damn brats… Just wait until they come back.”

[P156]
That was when a group of men caught Jang Il’s eye.

[P157]
Matching clothes and weapons, plus the slovenly air of men without discipline. It was a familiar sight.

[P158]
“Government troops.”

[P159]
Lately, government troops had become more common than neighborhood dogs.

[P160]
Normally, they slacked off so thoroughly that no one ever saw them, but now that the high and mighty had stepped in, they seemed to be scrambling to at least put on a show.

[P161]
*They said they were expanding the search area. Are they already this far out?*

[P162]
As he wondered about it, a middle-aged military officer who appeared to be leading the group approached him with a smile.

[P163]
“Are you, by any chance, a Beggars’ Sect disciple?”

[P164]
Jang Il nodded casually.

[P165]
“As you can see.”

[P166]
“I thought so when I saw your knots.”

[P167]
“Anyone can tell just by looking. Still, you’ve made good time. You’re already this far out.”

[P168]
“Ah, they say the Beggars’ Sect has the finest intelligence network under heaven. I suppose you already knew we were coming?”

[P169]
“This much is nothing out of the ordinary for our Sect.”

[P170]
The military officer smiled along with the smug Jang Il.

[P171]
“But there are no villages nearby, and hardly anyone passes through here. Why are you alone?”

[P172]
“Don’t get me started. The branch leader kept nagging me, so I brought a few men out to get some fresh air. Things have been a real mess lately with all this talk about a murderer.”

[P173]
“I see.”

[P174]
“Well, good luck with—”

[P175]
Jang Il never finished.

[P176]
The moment the officer nodded with a smile, something cold pierced his chest.

[P177]
Shnk!

[P178]
*…Huh?*

[P179]
Jang Il stared blankly at the sword buried in his chest and coughed up blood.

[P180]
Why?

[P181]
What for?

[P182]
The questions never escaped his lips. His knees buckled as he stared at the officer through clouding eyes.

[P183]
His face struck the new shoots just beginning to emerge from the earth, and a cold voice reached his ears.

[P184]
“Find the others. They should be nearby.”

[P185]
“As you command.”

[P186]
“Stupid beggar bastard. Why did he have to be here of all places…?”

[P187]
That was the last thing Jang Il heard.

[P188]
He was twenty-five years old.

[P189]
The young beggar died in a secluded forest two days from Emei Sect.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“……”

[P52]
“And you can’t have roast duck without liquor. Jiannan Chun, one of Sichuan’s finest! Meat and liquor are only fitting for a great hero like the Heavenly Power Demon, don’t you think?”

[P53]
“……”

[P54]
A frigid silence settled over the already chilly cell.

[P55]
I kept smiling brightly at the Heavenly Power Demon as he sat cross-legged. At last, I let out a deep sigh.

[P56]
“Fuck, I can’t do this anymore.”

[P57]
For three days, I’d bent over backward to please him. I’d softened my voice, spoken with scrupulous politeness, praised him as a Great Hero of benevolence and righteousness, and kissed his ass shamelessly.

[P58]
But the Heavenly Power Demon had refused every offer and comfort I provided. No matter how much food or clothing I brought him, he never touched any of it.

[P59]
“I’ve done more than enough by now. Are you really going to keep this up?”

[P60]
“……”

[P61]
“I’m only being this courteous because I’m such a gentleman. What do you think will happen if the Sichuan Tang Clan finds out, huh?”

[P62]
At that moment, the Heavenly Power Demon finally spoke without opening his eyes. It was the first time I’d heard his voice in three whole days, and it had grown terribly hoarse.

[P63]
“Tell them.”

[P64]
“What?”

[P65]
“This old man has endured enough torture to be sick of it. Even if I depart this world, I will have no regrets.”

[P66]
He had spent more than forty years imprisoned in the underground prison. Faced with his serene detachment, like some enlightened monk, I clicked my tongue.

[P67]
“Good grief. You really don’t listen, do you? Is it so difficult to tell me what you know about Dark Heaven?”

[P68]
“I have said all there is to say. Kill this old man or torture him. Do as you please.”

[P69]
“What kind of stubborn old man are you?”

[P70]
But the Heavenly Power Demon had already sealed his lips again. He probably wouldn’t open them a second time.

[P71]
“…Stubborn old bastard.”

[P72]
I heaved a sigh deep enough to sink the earth, placed the liquor and roast duck within his reach, and turned away.

[P73]
“Fine. For now, just eat that. You haven’t had anything in three days.”

[P74]
Even as I spoke, I knew. Whether I returned tomorrow, the day after, or three days from now, the food would still be exactly where I’d left it, stone cold and untouched.

[P75]
“Damn it.”

[P76]
With the Heavenly Power Demon fed—or at least served—I finished my rounds and dropped to the floor in a corridor far from the cells.

[P77]
*The Heavenly Power Demon.*

[P78]
His rigid face and that indescribable look in his eyes kept flashing through my mind. There was no mistaking the agitation those two words—*Dark Heaven*—had stirred in him.

[P79]
The problem was that he refused to say a word about it.

[P80]
*But he definitely knew about Dark Heaven long ago.*

[P81]
I hadn’t heard him admit it himself, but it was already as good as established fact.

[P82]
The real question was how he knew about Dark Heaven, and how much he knew.

[P83]
I slowly retraced the conversation I’d had with the Heavenly Power Demon three days ago.

[P84]
After putting the brain that had earned me Grade 7 school marks into overdrive, I arrived at a single plausible conclusion.

[P85]
*Dark Heaven and the Demonic Cult are deeply connected.*

[P86]
No. They might even be one and the same.

[P87]
The Heavenly Power Demon had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult. Even after forty years of imprisonment and torture, he had never lost his loyalty to the Cult.

[P88]
His silence was proof enough.

[P89]
*If Dark Heaven were an enemy of the Demonic Cult, he would’ve talked by now.*

[P90]
Then what the hell was Dark Heaven? Some splinter faction that had broken away from the Demonic Cult? Or another organization created within the Demonic Cult itself?

[P91]
*Like a Shincheonji branch called Sick-cheonji. Something like that.*

[P92]
Whatever they were, one thing was certain: the bastards were a plague.

[P93]
I’d been lost in thought for quite some time when Cheongpung appeared with a spring in his step, trailing a sweet aroma behind him.

[P94]
“Hey!”

[P95]
“…Your grandpa lives on Lotus Peak at Huashan, right?”

[P96]
Cheongpung swallowed what was in his mouth before answering.

[P97]
“No! He’s in Henan right now!”

[P98]
“Yeah, sure.”

[P99]
Why did I even bother talking to him?

[P100]
The mountain of food piled in Cheongpung’s arms left me speechless. I was starting to feel sorry for the former imperial chef, and I’d never even seen the man’s face.

[P101]
“You went out for all this?”

[P102]
“Yes! And while I was at it, I brought a letter from the Beggars’ Sect.”

[P103]
“…Shouldn’t that be the other way around?”

[P104]
“Hehe.”

[P105]
“Don’t smile. I might get attached.”

[P106]
I answered gruffly and accepted the letter Cheongpung held out.

[P107]
When I unfolded the grimy paper—wherever he’d been keeping it, it couldn’t have been clean—three strands of yellow dog hair drifted out.

[P108]
*A three-knot Disciple. The branch leader sent it.*

[P109]
Just as I’d expected, the letter was addressed to Gung Gibang from the Beggars’ Sect’s Chengdu branch leader.

[P110]
Of course, Gung Gibang was at the Divine Physician’s secret refuge, so the branch leader had probably sent it to me for convenience.

[P111]
A moment later, when I looked up from the letter, Cheongpung asked, “What does it say?”

[P112]
“Nothing much. They’re still searching.”

[P113]
The Beggars’ Sect had originally combed through Sichuan with a fine-tooth comb in search of the Divine Physician, but it had since changed targets.

[P114]
Now it was hunting the culprit who had murdered the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.

[P115]
*Not that a man like that would be easy to catch.*

[P116]
Tang Sadok had initially insisted on settling the matter with the Sichuan Tang Clan’s strength alone, but his attitude had changed after he lent me the Myriad-Poison Ring.

[P117]
Yet even with the Tang Clan’s full cooperation, the culprit’s trail had vanished like a ghost.

[P118]
“Do you think they’ll find him?”

[P119]
“Who knows? We’ll have to hope for the best. We have the Beggars’ Sect, and the Tang Clan’s Green Shadow Squad are experts in reconnaissance and pursuit. Surely they’ll turn up something.”

[P120]
“What about the government troops?”

[P121]
“They seem to be pulling their weight too.”

[P122]
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, wielded tremendous influence.

[P123]
Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, had readily agreed to my request to search for the culprit instead of the Divine Physician.

[P124]
The individual fighting ability of the government troops couldn’t compare to that of Murim warriors, but their sheer numbers—several thousand men—couldn’t be ignored.

[P125]
“Wow! Thousands?”

[P126]
“I don’t know the exact number, but apparently they’re swarming all over the place. You saw the government troops too, didn’t you, Young Hero Cheong? On our way back to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P127]
“Oh, but there weren’t that many when I saw them.”

[P128]
“…Of course not. Did you think thousands of men would all travel together?”

[P129]
It wasn’t hard to picture the government troops conducting inspections and searches in small groups according to their assigned formations.

[P130]
> The government troops are gradually expanding their search area and advancing toward Qingcheng and Emei.
>
> They appear to be searching for the culprit while preparing for a possible incident.

[P131]
I read the last line of the letter and let out a quiet laugh.

[P132]
*They’re doing better than I expected.*

[P133]
Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, looked every inch the corrupt official, but apparently he wasn’t completely incompetent. Either that, or the military officer in charge of this operation knew what he was doing.

[P134]
*But what if they still can’t find him after all this?*

[P135]
I’d talked a big game in front of Tang Sadok, so the thought was seriously worrying.

[P136]
Of course, Jeok Cheongang’s safe recovery came first.

[P137]
I glanced at the treatment room, whose door remained firmly shut, then casually asked Cheongpung, “What kind of food did you bring?”

[P138]
“Sho mush!”

[P139]
“…Finish what’s already in your mouth. I’ll just look for myself.”

[P140]
* * *

[P141]
Jang Il was a two-knot Disciple of the Beggars’ Sect.

[P142]
He had become one out of necessity rather than choice. He’d heard a rumor that anyone who formally joined the Beggars’ Sect, underwent the initiation ceremony, and became an official Disciple would receive a whole dumpling.

[P143]
What could an eight-year-old beggar brat who hadn’t eaten in four days have known?

[P144]
Clutching his empty stomach, he had gone to the Chengdu branch and become a Beggars’ Sect disciple that very day.

[P145]
“They only gave me half a dumpling, too. Just thinking about it still makes me grind my teeth. Goddamn bastards.”

[P146]
The beggars listening to Jang Il yawned quietly. They’d already heard the story dozens of times.

[P147]
More than ten years had passed, but Jang Il’s anger had yet to subside.

[P148]
“I gritted my teeth over that half dumpling and worked my way up to deputy branch leader. So you lot should…”

[P149]
As the story showed signs of dragging on, the three one-knot Disciples exchanged glances.

[P150]
“Oh! My stomach!”

[P151]
“Gasp! Mine too!”

[P152]
“Ugh, the latrine! Where’s the latrine?”

[P153]
“You little bastards!”

[P154]
Jang Il shouted, but the three beggars had already bolted.

[P155]
“Those damn brats… Just wait until they come back.”

[P156]
That was when a group of men caught Jang Il’s eye.

[P157]
Matching clothes and weapons, plus the slovenly air of men without discipline. It was a familiar sight.

[P158]
“Government troops.”

[P159]
Lately, government troops had become more common than neighborhood dogs.

[P160]
Normally, they slacked off so thoroughly that no one ever saw them, but now that the high and mighty had stepped in, they seemed to be scrambling to at least put on a show.

[P161]
*They said they were expanding the search area. Are they already this far out?*

[P162]
As he wondered about it, a middle-aged military officer who appeared to be leading the group approached him with a smile.

[P163]
“Are you, by any chance, a Beggars’ Sect disciple?”

[P164]
Jang Il nodded casually.

[P165]
“As you can see.”

[P166]
“I thought so when I saw your knots.”

[P167]
“Anyone can tell just by looking. Still, you’ve made good time. You’re already this far out.”

[P168]
“Ah, they say the Beggars’ Sect has the finest intelligence network under heaven. I suppose you already knew we were coming?”

[P169]
“This much is nothing out of the ordinary for our Sect.”

[P170]
The military officer smiled along with the smug Jang Il.

[P171]
“But there are no villages nearby, and hardly anyone passes through here. Why are you alone?”

[P172]
“Don’t get me started. The branch leader kept nagging me, so I brought a few men out to get some fresh air. Things have been a real mess lately with all this talk about a murderer.”

[P173]
“I see.”

[P174]
“Well, good luck with—”

[P175]
Jang Il never finished.

[P176]
The moment the officer nodded with a smile, something cold pierced his chest.

[P177]
Shnk!

[P178]
*…Huh?*

[P179]
Jang Il stared blankly at the sword buried in his chest and coughed up blood.

[P180]
Why?

[P181]
What for?

[P182]
The questions never escaped his lips. His knees buckled as he stared at the officer through clouding eyes.

[P183]
His face struck the new shoots just beginning to emerge from the earth, and a cold voice reached his ears.

[P184]
“Find the others. They should be nearby.”

[P185]
“As you command.”

[P186]
“Stupid beggar bastard. Why did he have to be here of all places…?”

[P187]
That was the last thing Jang Il heard.

[P188]
He was twenty-five years old.

[P189]
The young beggar died in a secluded forest two days from Emei Sect.

- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.

## Terminology

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
